subject: Extension economics: bridging plan + pilot credits
messages:
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: alex.ramos@sable.ai, procurement@sable.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Extension economics: bridging plan + pilot credits

Alex / procurement team —

Thanks again for taking the time this morning. Based on the usage traces we reviewed, Sable's production call mix is trending 28% higher than the forecast used for the Q3 contract, mostly from increased streaming/long-context usage in the recommendations path. That explains the token variance you saw in May. I've attached a lightweight breakdown (usage_report_May2027.csv) and a short performance snapshot.

Proposal (short):
- 3 month bridging extension from 2027-07-01 to 2027-09-30 to avoid a hard cutover during your holiday launch window.
- Provide a 20% pilot credit on incremental tokens above your current commit for the first 60 days of the extension (applies only to text-generation tokens).
- Canary SLA lane: prioritize a shard set with 99th percentile latency target of 220ms for the recommendation route (we can scope latency uplift on the May sample).
- Optional dedicated throughput burst for the launch window (pre-warm + 48h buffer).

Next steps I suggest: I can ship a one-page mutual action plan and a pricing addendum by EOD tomorrow, and legal can produce a short-term extension addendum. If procurement wants a consolidated PO, indicate the procurement contact and timing and I'll loop in finance.

Attachments: usage_report_May2027.csv, redwood_performance_snapshot_May2027.pdf

Cheers,

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0127

Redwood Inference — Developer-first inference runtime
From: alex.ramos@sable.ai
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@sable.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-21T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Extension economics: bridging plan + pilot credits

Jonas —

Appreciate the quick analysis. The May spike aligns with a mid-month recommender rollout we did; good to see the numbers match up. Procurement is watching budget but we want to avoid flapping the model in July. The bridging extension sounds reasonable. A few quick asks before we run this up the chain:

1) Can you quantify the expected monthly spend under the extension with and without the 20% pilot credit (ballpark numbers are fine)?
2) We need a short description of what the 99th percentile SLA buys us operationally (i.e., which endpoints will be shifted and what rollback looks like).
3) Procurement would prefer a single PO/short addendum vs a multi-page contract for this short window.

If you can send a one-pager and a simple PO-friendly addendum, I can push this through budget review early next week (Mon/Tue). Also copying procurement for timing.

Thanks —
Alex Ramos
Head of Platform Engineering, Sable AI
alex.ramos@sable.ai
From: jonas_weber@redwood.com
To: alex.ramos@sable.ai, procurement@sable.ai
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com
Date: 2027-06-22T08:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Extension economics: bridging plan + pilot credits

Alex — all good, answers below and attaching a concise bridge_proposal_v1.pdf that matches the asks. Quick summary inline: 

1) Spend scenarios (estimates based on May mix and +15% / +30% demand scenarios):
   - Baseline (no extension, pro-rated): $42k/month
   - Extension w/o credit (expected footprint): $54k/month
   - Extension w/ 20% pilot credit on incremental tokens: ~ $47k/month effective for months 1-2
   - Conservative surge (30%): $72k/month w/ credit ~ $62k/month

2) 99th percentile SLA summary (operational impact):
   - What it buys: lower tail latency for production recommendation calls by routing them to a prioritized shard pool and enabling pre-warmed KV cache retention for pinned contexts. We guarantee prioritized scheduling for 'recommendation' route only — other routes stay on standard lanes.
   - Fallback: if prioritized lanes exceed safe headroom, requests automatically fall back to standard lanes (no request loss) and an incident alert is created; we provide immediate scale-up options (burst capacity) under the extension.

3) PO/addendum approach: happy to use a one-page addendum + PO. I included a proposed line-item for the pilot credit and a short mutual action plan in the attached PDF. DocuSign link is here: https://docusign.com/AAABBB-CCCDD-7842

Timing: if procurement can confirm by Tue 2027-06-28, we can enable the extension starting 2027-07-01 and kick off the canary.

If you'd like, we can run a 30-minute ops walkthrough Tuesday to show the prioritized lane behavior on your sample traffic. Available slots: Tue 10:00–11:00 or 14:00–14:30 PT.

Regards,

Jonas Weber
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com

Attachments: bridge_proposal_v1.pdf
From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, hannah_schmitt@redwood.com

Subject: Fwd: Extension economics: bridging plan + pilot credits — legal/finance prep

Jonas / Hannah —

Looping in legal (Soojin) to prepare the short addendum and finance to review PO flow. Notes for the addendum:
- Term: 2027-07-01 to 2027-09-30, auto-expire unless renewed.
- Pilot credit: 20% applied to incremental tokens above the baseline for the first 60 days; specify line-item and start date.
- SLA: include prioritized lane description and rollback/automatic fallback clause.

Kim will confirm exact accounting code and invoice cadence once procurement confirms PO. Please attach the finalized usage CSV in the legal ticket.
